blocks.value: Web design is basically the skill that helps create websites, that means it decides how a website looks, how it feels, how people will move from one page to another, and how comfortable and enjoyable the whole online experience will be. In simple words, web design is like designing a house, but instead of walls and floors, you use colours, shapes, layouts, images, and computer code.

A Web design course teaches students how to create websites from the basic level to the advanced level. Many students believe that web design is very technical but in reality, it is a very creative field. You don’t need to be a computer genius to learn it. Even a student who knows basic computer skills can easily study this course.

Web Design admission is based on both the entrance and Class 12 scores. You need to pass Class 12 with 50% to be eligbile. Exams are JEECUP, CUET, etc. P opular colleges are World University of Design, JD Institute of Fashion Technology, Hans Raj Mahila Maha Vidyalaya, etc. The fee can range around approx. faqs.question: What is the difference between Java and JavaScript?
faqs.answer: The two languages are completely unrelated. JavaScript was originally called Livescript, and was renamed when Java was introduced as a kind of cross-marketing. There was some hope that they'd be used together and evolve together. They never really were; Java applets never took off. Some of the key differences are mentioned below : 1. Java is an OOP programming language while JavaScript is an OOP scripting language. 2. Java creates applications that run in a virtual machine or browser while JavaScript code is run on a browser only. 3. Java code needs to be compiled while JavaScript code are all in text. 4. They require different plug-ins. All the best

faqs.question: What should I do to become a professional web designer?
faqs.answer: Web designers and web developers are two of the most sought-after professions these days, and it's not as hard as it may seem to become one. One needs to work in an efficient and a well-planned manner. - Learning the programming languages: *Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is what controls the content and layout of what you see in your web browser. *JavaScript is the language of the web, all major web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, IE, and many more) have JavaScript support built in. *CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. Its used to customize the look and feel of the HTML elements on your page. These are the important languages that one needs to know which makes you professional. The other fundamental languages include C, C+, Java, C#, Python, Ruby, etc. - The next step is to complete one or two personal projects, to get comfortable building things from end to end. Then enhance yourself by making projects for others or by innovating on your own. - To get a good job, build a strong resume. This makes you more confident in attending Interviews and getting a job. 4)Once you start working for a company, you will gradually increase your real-time work experience thereby increasing your reputation as well as salary. This would also make you get still better jobs. All the best!

faqs.question: What is the difference between UX and UI designer and web designer?
faqs.answer: There is a huge difference between UX and UI designer and a web designer. A UX and UI designer needs to hold an expertise on developing wireframes, by which we mean if a project proposal has been kept in front of you, you need to study the proposal and develop a basic skeletal structure of view ability of that project for example: how should the logo appear and what shall be the suitable logo design look like, where and how are the components on a web page going to be oriented like the position of buttons, form fields length and breadth, carousel relevance if any etc. Such that the web page produced is appealing and accessible for the user in the easiest manner without any complications, you may have to design a sitemap and user guide for a complex application along with usage of tools like Photoshop, Illustrator and Core draw to give an attractive look to your developed skeletal structure and then you need to convert these PSD (Photoshop produced) files to basic HTML, CSS and Bootstrap code in the exact way. Whereas a web designer does not deal with creating skeletal structures and PSD files but only deals with the designs he has obtained from the UX and UI team and converts it into HTML CSS Bootstrap code along with Javascript and Query functional validations and dynamicity provision for your web pages and now-a-days angular framework to manage most of the dynamic functionality of your webiste via design itself reducing backed chaos.

Web Design includes areas like web graphic design , user interface design (UI design), user experience design (UX Design), standardised code, authoring and Search Engine Optimization (SEO) . Web Design involves the design process related to the front-end of the website. Generally, Web Designers use vector and raster graphics to create their design prototypes. There are huge career opportunities in the field of Web Design. Students can pursue Undergraduate, Diploma and online Certification courses in Web Design as per their interest and ability. Types of Web Design Courses

The Web Design course is designed in a way that it can cater to all types of candidates. Candidates should check out the eligibility criteria and scope before selecting any course. Some important facts regarding the Web Design are mentioned below:

Web Design degree course: A full-time undergraduate degree course in Web Design is a three-year duration course spread across six semesters. It is the most sought-after choice for Web Design applicants. The programme includes physical classrooms, assessments, internships and final placements.
Web Design diploma courses: The diploma courses are of two-years duration. These courses consist of practical assignments and internships. Some design institutes offer placements as well.

Online Web Design courses: Online Web Design courses has gained a lot of prominence in recent years. The aim of introducing an online course was to provide the students with the opportunity to pursue the course via a virtual education system. There are no physical classrooms or interactions and the lectures are held using online video conferencing. The notes and study materials are shared on the internet through various mediums. There are many online platforms that provide Web Design certifications.

value: BTech in Web Designing: Students of computer science and information technology study web designing as a part of their courses. These courses offer students the opportunity to explore different aspects of web development by teaching them various programming languages.

BSc in Web Designing: Like BTech, students opting for BSc in computer science and information technology, learn web designing as a part of their course as well. Although both the courses focus on different aspects, web designing remains common for both.

BSc in Web Development: BSc in web development is focused primarily on programming languages such as HTML, CSS , Javascript, Java , or XML. This course also provides students with knowledge of Internet marketing, advertising , and web applications. This three-year course in web development includes System Design, Internet Law, Image Editing, HTML, CSS, and Java Programming, E-commerce , and Graphic Design.

Diploma in Web Designing: This course has a duration of 1-2 years, and the students opting for the same are exposed to a wide range of technologies with a major focus on programming languages, front-end and client-side scripting languages, such as HTML5/CSS and JavaScript. Online Web Designing Courses and Certifications: Many colleges and online learning platforms offer students and enthusiasts an opportunity to learn web designing. These courses have a duration ranging from a month to a year and not only help you learn the contents of the course but also provide certifications.

General examination pattern: Students are evaluated based on projects, assignments, mid-semester examinations, and end-semester examinations. However, evaluation is done based on one final examination for diploma and certification courses instead of mid and end semester examinations.

Students who cannot afford full-time courses due to time or eligibility, can opt for an online web designing course. Several institutions offer web designing courses to such students, and the duration of these courses ranges from a month to a year. All you need to learn web designing from such institutions is a computer and a strong internet connection.

The syllabus for these courses remains more or less the same. However, a course with a duration of a month would give you brief information and an introduction to web designing, and a course with a duration of a year will provide a detailed view. Although these courses have assignments to assimilate the students, unlike the full-time BTech and BSc courses, evaluation is done based on the final examination, for which a certificate of completion is also provided. These courses are recognised worldwide, and the valued certification holds weightage in building a strong portfolio.

intro: The process of creating a website, including its layout and content, is called Web Designing. Making a website look and feel better is the main goal of web designing. A web designer's job is to become well-versed in all aspects of websites before building one with eye-catching graphics and pertinent content.

At the entry level , the web designers can work to create visual and user experience components of websites and earn an average salary ranging from INR 4 to 5 lakh. However, the positions at the mid-senior level web designers are in charge of planning and carrying out online initiatives. They usually play a bigger part in client relations and project planning and earn a pay ranging from INR 8 to 10 lakh. questions.question_text: Is web design a good career choice?
questions.answer_text: Web design can be a great career if you enjoy mixing creativity with practical problem-solving. You get to make things that people actually use — beautiful pages that work well on phones and laptops, and that help a business or idea come alive. The learning curve is friendly (you can start with a few basics and keep growing), and there are plenty of freelance or full-time paths, so you can shape the job around your life. If you like design, learning new tools, and seeing immediate results from your work, give it a shot — it's rewarding and flexible.
As a simple answer I would like to tell you that I have seen more scope of web designing when compared to graphic designing.
